mainTopic: Mistaken egg sales, when an egg counts as laid, attached eggs as meat, and eggs found on יום טוב
overview: The amud opens by finishing two stories in which רבי אמי rules that selling eggs that cannot hatch to a buyer who wanted eggs that can hatch is a מקח טעות, and the sale is cancelled. Then the גמרא offers two readings of רב's phrase 'עם יציאתה נגמרה': either the egg counts as finished once most of it is out, like רבי יוחנן, or only once all of it is out. Next, with 'גופא', it examines a ברייתא: fully formed eggs found in a slaughtered hen may be eaten with milk, but רבי יעקב forbids them if they are still attached by sinews. The גמרא asks whether another ברייתא, about which parts of a dead kosher bird make the eater טמא, follows רבי יעקב. רב יוסף links it to רבי יעקב, and in both versions אביי shows the link is not proven. A ברייתא then teaches that a chicken mates and lays only by day. That supports רב מרי's ruling that an egg found at dawn on יום טוב, in a nest that was empty the evening before, is permitted. רב's opposite ruling is explained as speaking of an egg 'from the earth', which a hen does not form when a rooster is present. The amud ends as רב גמדא begins to say how close the rooster must be, and his answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Eggs of a live hen: רבי אמי voids the sale
steps.stepSummary: A buyer asked for eggs from a live hen but was given eggs from a slaughtered hen. רבי אמי ruled the sale is a מקח טעות and is undone.
steps.simpleTranslation: (A man was calling out: who has eggs) of a live hen? They gave him eggs of a slaughtered hen. He came before רבי אמי. רבי אמי said to them: it is a mistaken purchase, and it is undone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a story that began on the previous daf. A buyer got the wrong kind of eggs and went to רבי אמי, who cancelled the sale.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eggs from a living hen can hatch into chicks. Eggs taken from a hen after it was slaughtered cannot. Because the buyer clearly asked for one type and got another, רבי אמי calls it a מקח טעות, and the whole deal is reversed.

keyTerms.meaning: A slaughtered animal (here, a slaughtered hen)
A mistaken purchase, a sale based on an error, which is void
And it goes back; the sale is undone

steps.confusionAlert: This amud starts in the middle of a sentence. The words 'A man said: eggs...' are on the previous daf. So 'דפחיא למאן' means 'who has eggs of a live hen?'

phrases.english: (eggs) of a live hen, who has?
phrases.notes: Continues the buyer's call from the previous daf

phrases.english: They gave him eggs of a slaughtered hen.
He came before Rabbi Ami,

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: מִקָּח טָעוּת הוּא, וְהָדַר.
phrases.english: He said to them: it is a mistaken purchase, and it is reversed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אתא לקמיה דרבי אמי אמר להו מקח טעות הוא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a story begun on the previous daf
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Selling eggs of a slaughtered hen to someone who asked for eggs of a live hen is a מקח טעות, and the sale is void.

steps.title: Isn't this obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ruling: why would רבי אמי need to say something this obvious?
steps.simpleTranslation: It is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects that the ruling seems too obvious to need saying. This line sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The buyer clearly asked for one product and got another, so of course the sale is void. The גמרא assumes a recorded ruling must teach something new. It wants to know what that new point is.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious; a challenge asking why a ruling needed to be stated

phrases.english: It is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the ruling in Step 1
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אמי's ruling that the sale is a מקח טעות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The buyer named exactly what he wanted, so voiding the sale seems self-evident and not worth recording.

steps.title: We might have thought he only wanted eating eggs
steps.stepSummary: The ruling is needed. Otherwise we might think the buyer wanted the eggs for eating and only cared that live-hen eggs are firmer. In that case he would only get the price difference back.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: this man wants them for eating. And the reason he said 'of a live hen' is because those eggs are firmer. What difference does that make? Then they would just give him back the price difference between them. So רבי אמי teaches us that the sale is fully void.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the פשיטא question. It shows there was a reasonable alternative reading that רבי אמי's ruling rules out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the buyer only wanted eggs to eat, he received eggs, just slightly lower quality ones. Then the sale would stand and he would get a partial refund. רבי אמי teaches that we take him at his word: he wanted eggs that can hatch, so this is a different product and the whole sale is cancelled.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said; introduces a mistaken assumption
The difference in value between the two

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the difference between a full מקח טעות, which voids the sale, and a quality shortfall, which only gets a partial refund. That depends on what the buyer actually needed the item for.

phrases.english: You might have said:
this man wants them for eating,
and the fact that he said 'of a live hen'
is because they are firm,
what is the practical difference?
to give him back the difference in value,
it teaches us (that the sale is void).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא challenge of Step 2
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא: shows a reasonable mistaken assumption that the ruling corrects
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The buyer wanted eggs for eating and only preferred firmer eggs, so he would only get the price difference back.
steps.terutzMaskana: We assume he wanted eggs that hatch, so the sale is a full מקח טעות and is void.

steps.title: Eggs of a rooster: רבי אמי voids the sale again
steps.stepSummary: A buyer called out for fertilized eggs and was given unfertilized ones. רבי אמי again ruled it a מקח טעות.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain man called out: who has eggs fertilized by a rooster? Who has eggs fertilized by a rooster? They gave him eggs that the hen had absorbed from the ground (unfertilized). He came before רבי אמי, who said to them: it is a mistaken purchase, and it is undone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a second, parallel story with the same ruling from רבי אמי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eggs from a hen that mated with a rooster can hatch. Eggs formed without a rooster, which the hen 'absorbed from the ground', cannot. Again the buyer got a different product from what he asked for, so the sale is void.

keyTerms.meaning: That the hen absorbed from the ground; unfertilized eggs

phrases.english: A certain man said to them:
Eggs of a rooster, who has?
Eggs of a rooster, who has?
phrases.notes: The buyer repeats his call, as a street buyer would

phrases.english: They gave him eggs that the hen absorbed from the ground.
He came before Rabbi Ami,

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: מִקָּח טָעוּת הוּא, וַהֲדַר.
phrases.english: He said to them: it is a mistaken purchase, and it is reversed.

steps.triggerLanguage: ההוא דאמר להו ביעי דדכרא למאן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel case with the same structure as Step 1
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Giving unfertilized eggs to someone who asked for fertilized eggs is a מקח טעות, and the sale is void.

steps.title: Isn't this obvious too?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא again asks why such an obvious ruling needed to be stated.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the same challenge for the second story. It is setting up the explanation that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The buyer clearly said he wanted rooster eggs and got something else. Voiding the sale seems self-evident, so the גמרא asks what this story adds.

phrases.english: It is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the ruling in Step 4
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אמי's ruling in the rooster-egg case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The buyer specified fertilized eggs, so cancelling the sale seems too obvious to record.

steps.title: We might have thought he wanted fatter eggs to eat
steps.stepSummary: The ruling is needed. Otherwise we might think the buyer wanted eating eggs and only preferred rooster eggs because they are fatter, which would earn him only a partial refund.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: this man wants them for eating. And the reason he said 'of a rooster' is because those eggs are fatter. What difference does that make? Then they would just give him back the price difference. So רבי אמי teaches us that the sale is fully void.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the פשיטא question with the same kind of answer it gave for the first story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the guess is that fertilized eggs are richer and fatter, so maybe the buyer only wanted better eating eggs and deserves just the price difference. רבי אמי rejects that and treats the buyer as wanting eggs that hatch. That makes the sale a full מקח טעות.
steps.whatToRemember: In both stories the buyer asked for eggs that can hatch and got eggs that cannot. רבי אמי rules each a full מקח טעות, so the sale is cancelled. The גמרא explains that we might have thought the buyer only wanted better eating eggs and would only get the price difference back. The rulings teach that we take the buyer's request at face value.

phrases.english: You might have said:
this man wants them for eating,
and the fact that he said 'of a rooster'
is because they are fatter,
what is the practical difference?
to give him back the difference in value,
it teaches us (that the sale is void).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא challenge of Step 5, following the same pattern as Step 3
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא: shows a reasonable mistaken assumption that the ruling corrects
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The buyer wanted fatter eggs for eating, so he would only get the price difference back.
steps.terutzMaskana: We assume he wanted eggs that hatch, so the sale is a full מקח טעות and is void.

steps.title: A second reading: the egg is finished once most of it comes out
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers another way to explain רב's phrase 'עם יציאתה נגמרה.' It means the egg is finished once MOST of it has come out, in line with רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: what does 'it is finished with its emergence' mean? It is finished once most of it has come out, like רבי יוחנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, alternative explanation of רב's words about when an egg counts as 'finished.' It also sets up a quote from רבי יוחנן to back this reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key word is 'יציאתה,' meaning 'its coming out.' This reading says that 'coming out' does not have to be complete. Once most of the egg is out, it already counts as finished and born.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say: introduces an alternative answer
Its emergence (the egg coming out of the hen)

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
What does 'it is finished with its emergence' mean?
It is finished with the emergence of most of it,
and this is in line with Rabbi Yochanan.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the רבי אמי cases to offer an alternative reading of רב's phrase, which was explained earlier on the daf.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of a key word (יציאתה = emergence of most of the egg)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might read 'its emergence' as requiring the full, complete laying of the egg.
steps.terutzMaskana: In this reading, 'emergence' means most of the egg coming out, matching רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's ruling about an egg that mostly came out and went back in
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that if most of an egg came out on ערב יום טוב and then slipped back in, it may be eaten on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: For רבי יוחנן said: an egg, most of which came out on the eve of יום טוב and then went back in, may be eaten on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the source behind the previous reading. רבי יוחנן treats an egg that mostly came out before יום טוב as already laid before יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The egg was finally laid on יום טוב itself. Normally an egg laid on יום טוב is forbidden (it is נולד). But since most of it came out the day before, it counts as born on ערב יום טוב, so it is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: And it went back (into the hen)

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the principle 'רובו ככולו' (most counts like all) applied to the moment an egg is 'born.' That moment decides whether it is permitted on יום טוב.

phrases.english: For Rabbi Yochanan said:
An egg, most of which came out
on the eve of the festival, and then went back in
is permitted to be eaten on the festival.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the quoted ruling of רבי יוחנן that step 7 relied on.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An egg that mostly emerged on ערב יום טוב and went back in is permitted on יום טוב, because it counts as already born.

steps.title: Another version: the egg is finished only once all of it comes out
steps.stepSummary: A different version reports that רב's phrase means the egg is finished only when ALL of it has come out.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say: what does 'it is finished with its emergence' mean? It is finished once all of it has come out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different version of how to read רב's phrase. In this version, the egg counts as finished only when it has come out completely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the opposite reading of the same word 'יציאתה.' Here 'coming out' means full emergence, not just most of the egg.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say: introduces an alternate version

phrases.english: And some say:
What does 'it is finished with its emergence' mean?
It is finished with the emergence of all of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a competing version against step 7's 'most of it' reading.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב's phrase means the egg is finished only upon complete emergence.

steps.title: This version rejects רבי יוחנן's 'most of it' rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws the inference: all of it, yes; most of it, no. This version of רב therefore excludes רבי יוחנן's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once all of it came out, yes. But if only most of it came out, no. This comes to reject the view of רבי יוחנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out what the 'all of it' version means in practice. An egg that only mostly came out does not count as finished, which disagrees with רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'כולה' (all of it) is read precisely, so 'רובה' (most of it) is shut out. In this version, the egg in רבי יוחנן's case would not count as laid before יום טוב. רב and רבי יוחנן would then disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude / to reject (a certain view)

steps.whatToRemember: There are two versions of רב's phrase. Version 1: 'most of the egg out' is enough, matching רבי יוחנן. Version 2: the whole egg must be out, rejecting רבי יוחנן.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two versions. They read the same words 'עם יציאתה נגמרה' in opposite ways. The first agrees with רבי יוחנן, and the second disagrees with him.

phrases.english: With the emergence of all of it, yes,
but with most of it, no.
And this comes to exclude the view of Rabbi Yochanan.

steps.triggerLanguage: עִם יְצִיאַת כּוּלָּהּ אִין אֲבָל רוּבָּהּ לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the practical consequence of step 9's reading and contrasts it with step 8.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In the second version, an egg counts as finished only when fully out, against רבי יוחנן's 'most of it' rule.

steps.title: Fully formed eggs found in a slaughtered hen may be eaten with milk
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to a ברייתא quoted earlier: one who slaughters a hen and finds fully formed eggs inside may eat them with milk.
steps.simpleTranslation: The matter itself: someone who slaughters a hen and finds fully formed eggs inside it may eat them with milk.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new section with 'גופא.' It goes back to quote and analyze a ברייתא that was mentioned earlier in passing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fully formed eggs inside the hen are treated as eggs, not as meat. So the laws of בשר בחלב do not apply to them, and they may be eaten with milk.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter itself: the גמרא returns to examine a source it quoted earlier

phrases.english: The matter itself:
One who slaughters a hen
and finds fully formed eggs inside it,
they are permitted to be eaten with milk.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, analyzing the ברייתא about eggs found in a slaughtered hen.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fully formed eggs found inside a slaughtered hen are not meat and may be eaten with milk.

steps.title: רבי יעקב: eggs still attached by sinews are forbidden with milk
steps.stepSummary: רבי יעקב disagrees in part. If the eggs are still attached to the hen by sinews, they are forbidden with milk.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יעקב says: if they were still attached by sinews, they are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: Within the same ברייתא, רבי יעקב adds a limit to the first ruling. Eggs still connected to the hen's body by sinews count as part of the meat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether attachment makes the eggs part of the bird's flesh. רבי יעקב says it does, so they take on the status of meat and cannot be eaten with milk.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yaakov says:
If they were attached by sinews,
they are forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A dissenting opinion within the same ברייתא as step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eggs still attached by sinews count as meat and are forbidden with milk.

steps.title: Which תנא holds that eating attached eggs from a bird's carcass leaves one pure?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא taught a ברייתא listing parts of a kosher bird's נבילה that do not make the eater טמא. The list includes a cluster of eggs, bones, sinews, and flesh torn from a live animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who taught what the רבנן taught in a ברייתא: one who eats from the נבילה of a kosher bird, from the cluster of eggs, from the bones, from the sinews, or from flesh torn off a living animal, remains טהור?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks who is the author of a ברייתא that treats a cluster of eggs as not part of the bird's meat. It is setting up an answer that will link this ברייתא to the dispute just quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eating נבילת עוף טהור normally makes a person טמא. This ברייתא says the egg cluster does not, so it must hold that attached eggs are not meat. That sounds like the ת"ק and not רבי יעקב, so the גמרא wants to identify the author.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is the תנא (author) of this teaching?
The carcass of a kosher bird that was not properly slaughtered
A cluster of developed eggs still attached by sinews inside the bird
That was torn off a living animal

steps.confusionAlert: This ברייתא is about טומאה (ritual impurity), not about eating with milk. The גמרא connects the two because both depend on the same question: are attached eggs considered meat?

phrases.english: Who is the tanna who taught
this, which the Rabbis taught:
One who eats from the carcass of a kosher bird,
from the cluster of eggs,
from the bones, and from the sinews,
and from the flesh that was torn off a living animal,
is pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the dispute in steps 11 and 12 to ask about the author of a related ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the תנא who holds that the egg cluster of a kosher bird's נבילה does not make the eater טמא.

steps.title: The second half of the list: parts that do make the eater impure
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes its list. Eating from the ovary of tiny eggs, the gizzard, or the intestines, or swallowing melted fat, makes a person טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: However, if he ate from the ovary of tiny eggs, from the gizzard or the intestines, or if he melted the fat and swallowed it, he is impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא from the previous step continues. Now it lists the parts of the bird that DO make the eater טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half of the list (step 13) gave parts that do not make one טמא, including the cluster of developed eggs. Here the ovary of tiny, undeveloped eggs is treated as real flesh of the bird, so it does make one טמא. Fat counts too, even when melted into liquid and swallowed.

keyTerms.meaning: The ovary: a cluster of tiny, undeveloped eggs, treated as flesh of the bird

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up אשכול (ovary of tiny eggs, which makes one טמא) with שלל (cluster of developed eggs, which is טהור). The next step asks about the שלל.

phrases.english: from the ovary of eggs (the tiny undeveloped ones),
from the gizzard and the intestines,
or if he melted the fat and swallowed it —
he is impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא quoted in step 13
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ovary of tiny eggs, the gizzard, the intestines, and melted fat of a kosher bird's נבילה all make the eater טמא.

steps.title: Which תנא says the cluster of eggs is pure?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose opinion the ברייתא follows when it rules that the cluster of developed eggs is טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is the תנא who taught that one who eats from the cluster of eggs is pure?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask whose view this ruling matches. This sets up the next step, where an answer is offered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calling the cluster טהור means the ברייתא treats these attached eggs as separate from the bird's flesh. רבי יעקב (step 12) said attached eggs count as meat for milk purposes. So the question is whether the ברייתא can fit his view.

keyTerms.meaning: A cluster of developed eggs still inside the hen

phrases.english: Who is the Tanna who taught:
"from the cluster of eggs, he is pure"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks whose view the ברייתא's ruling follows
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that the cluster of attached eggs is not part of the bird for טומאה purposes.

steps.title: רב יוסף: Not רבי יעקב
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says the ברייתא cannot follow רבי יעקב, because רבי יעקב treats eggs attached by sinews as meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: It is not like רבי יעקב. For if it were like רבי יעקב, he said: if they were attached by sinews, they are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers the question. Whoever taught this ברייתא, it was not רבי יעקב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יעקב forbids attached eggs with milk, so he must view them as part of the bird's meat. If they are meat, they should also make the eater טמא like the rest of the נבילה. Since the ברייתא calls them טהור, רב יוסף concludes that it disagrees with רבי יעקב.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
It is not in accordance with Rabbi Ya'akov.
For if it were like Rabbi Ya'akov, didn't he say:
"If they were attached by sinews, they are forbidden"!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שאלה of step 15
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא does not follow רבי יעקב, since he treats attached eggs as meat.

steps.title: אביי: רבי יעקב may have spoken only about milk
steps.stepSummary: אביי argues that רבי יעקב's ruling may apply only to the איסור of eating the eggs with milk, not to טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: From where do you know this? Perhaps רבי יעקב said it there only regarding the prohibition, but regarding impurity, no.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on רב יוסף. He says the ברייתא could still match רבי יעקב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף assumed that 'meat for milk' automatically means 'meat for טומאה.' אביי breaks that link. רבי יעקב may have been strict about milk only, so he could agree that the eggs are טהור.

keyTerms.meaning: He only said it up to here (his ruling is limited)

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not saying the eggs are not meat at all. He is saying the same eggs can be treated one way for milk and another way for טומאה.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him: From where do you know?
Perhaps he only said it
(Rabbi Ya'akov, there)
only with regard to the prohibition,
but with regard to impurity — no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב יוסף's inference in step 16
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the ברייתא must disagree with רבי יעקב
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב יוסף wrongly assumed that a ruling about milk carries over to טומאה.

steps.title: Anticipated objection: Let us decree impurity too
steps.stepSummary: אביי raises a possible objection. Perhaps רבי יעקב would also make a decree to be strict about טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say: regarding impurity, let us also make a decree —
steps.whatsHappening: אביי anticipates a challenge to his own point. This sets up his answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge says: if רבי יעקב is strict about milk, he should also be strict about טומאה and call the eggs part of the bird. That would bring back רב יוסף's conclusion.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (an anticipated objection)
Let us make a rabbinic decree

phrases.english: And if you will say:
regarding impurity, let us also decree —

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא לְעִנְיַן טוּמְאָה נָמֵי נִגְזוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Anticipates a challenge to אביי's distinction
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's split between milk and טומאה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If strictness applies to milk, a decree could extend it to טומאה as well.

steps.title: We do not add rabbinic impurity
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that such a decree would only increase טומאה, and we do not increase rabbinic טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: That would be increasing impurity, and we do not increase impurity by rabbinic law.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the objection. The rabbis do not invent extra rabbinic rules that make more things טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being strict about milk keeps a person away from a possible איסור. Being strict about טומאה would just make more things impure, and the rabbis avoid doing that. So רבי יעקב can forbid the eggs with milk and still call them טהור, and the ברייתא can follow his view.
steps.whatToRemember: רב יוסף said the ברייתא is not like רבי יעקב. אביי showed it could be: רבי יעקב's strictness about milk does not carry over to טומאה. That is because the rabbis do not create more rabbinic impurity.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule 'we do not increase rabbinic טומאה' is a general principle. It shows that a strict ruling in one area of הלכה does not automatically carry over to another.

phrases.english: that would be increasing impurity,
and we do not increase impurity by rabbinic law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the anticipated objection of step 18
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A strict decree about milk should extend to טומאה as well.
steps.terutzMaskana: Rabbinic decrees are not used to increase טומאה, so רבי יעקב can agree the eggs are טהור.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ברייתא can follow רבי יעקב: attached eggs are forbidden with milk but do not make the eater טמא.

steps.title: A second version asks who taught that the egg cluster makes one impure
steps.stepSummary: In a second version (איכא דאמרי), the גמרא asks which תנא holds that eating from the egg cluster of a dead bird makes a person טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say the discussion went like this: Who is the תנא who taught that one who eats from the cluster of eggs is impure?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives a different version of the earlier discussion. This is the setup question that opens the new version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same ברייתא from steps 13–14. The first version asked about its טהור clause (the שלל of eggs). This version asks instead about its טמא clause (the אשכול of eggs): whose opinion treats the אשכול as meat of the נבלה?

keyTerms.meaning: Who is the תנא? This asks whose opinion a teaching follows.

steps.confusionAlert: The two versions do not quote different ברייתות. Both use the same ברייתא, which says the שלל is טהור and the אשכול is טמא. The first version asks who wrote the שלל clause. The second asks who wrote the אשכול clause, and רב יוסף reads אשכול as the eggs hanging from the ovary.

phrases.english: And some say:
phrases.notes: This brings a second version of the earlier discussion.

phrases.english: Who is the tanna [who taught]
[that one who eats] from the ovary of eggs is impure?
phrases.notes: This is the part of the ברייתא about the אשכול (Step 14), from the נבלה of a kosher bird.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This restarts the sugya of Step 15 in a second version, which focuses on the ברייתא's אשכול (טמא) clause from Step 14 instead of the שלל (טהור) clause.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that the egg cluster counts as meat, so that eating it makes one טמא.

steps.title: רב יוסף says it follows רבי יעקב
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that the ברייתא follows רבי יעקב, who said that eggs attached by sinews are forbidden, meaning they count as meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: It is רבי יעקב, who said: If the eggs were attached by sinews, they are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף names the תנא behind the ברייתא. It is רבי יעקב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף reads 'אשכול' as the eggs hanging from the ovary, still attached by sinews. רבי יעקב treats such eggs as meat, so they are forbidden with milk. If they count as meat, they should also make one טמא like the rest of the נבלה, which matches the ברייתא's אשכול clause.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
It is Rabbi Ya'akov, who said:
If they were attached by sinews, they are forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא follows רבי יעקב, because he treats attached eggs as meat.

steps.title: אביי says the cluster may mean the ovary itself
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects the proof. Maybe the ברייתא is talking about the ovary itself, not the eggs hanging from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: How do you know that 'cluster' means the eggs hanging on the cluster? Perhaps it means the cluster itself.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges how רב יוסף read the ברייתא. He says the word 'cluster' could mean the ovary tissue itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the ברייתא means the ovary itself, that tissue is plain meat according to everyone. Then the ברייתא tells us nothing about attached eggs, and there is no proof that it follows רבי יעקב.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do you know? It questions an assumption.
Cluster. Here it means the ovary of a bird, where the eggs grow.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
From where [do you know] that 'cluster' [means]
from those [eggs] that hang on the cluster?
Perhaps [it means] the cluster itself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב יוסף's identification in Step 21 by reading the ברייתא differently.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof that the ברייתא follows רבי יעקב. The ruling of the ברייתא itself is not rejected.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב יוסף assumed 'cluster' means the attached eggs, but it could mean the ovary itself.

steps.title: Why would the ברייתא need to say the ovary is meat
steps.stepSummary: אביי raises a possible objection to his own reading. If the ברייתא means the ovary itself, that is obviously meat, so why say it?
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say: If it means the cluster itself, why does it need to be said?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי anticipates a problem with his reading. This line sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ovary is body tissue of the bird, so it is plainly meat. A ברייתא does not usually teach something obvious. That seems to weaken אביי's reading.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you say. This introduces an expected objection.
Why say it? It is obvious.

phrases.english: And if you say:
The cluster itself, what is there to say [about it]!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא: אֶשְׁכּוֹל גּוּפֵיהּ מַאי לְמֵימְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's alternate reading from Step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's reading that the ברייתא refers to the ovary itself.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ovary is obviously meat, so the ברייתא would be teaching something that needs no teaching.

steps.title: Like the gizzard and intestines, some people do not eat it
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the ovary is like the gizzard and intestines. Even though they are meat, some people do not eat them, so the ברייתא needed to teach that they count as meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is just like the gizzard and the intestines. Even though they are meat, since some people do not eat them, it was necessary to teach us. Here too, since some people do not eat it, it was necessary to teach us.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the objection by comparing the ovary to the gizzard and intestines. This keeps his reading of the ברייתא alive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Something can be meat by law and still not be eaten by many people. That could make us think it does not count as food. So the ברייתא has to say clearly that the ovary has the status of meat, and the proof for רבי יעקב falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: Just as it is with. This introduces a comparison.
It was necessary to teach us

steps.whatToRemember: In this second version, אביי again blocks רב יוסף. The ברייתא can be read as talking about the ovary itself, which is meat for everyone, so it does not have to follow רבי יעקב.

phrases.english: Just as it is with the gizzard and the intestines,
that even though they are meat,
since there are people who do not eat [them],
it was necessary to teach us;
here too:
since there are people who do not eat [it],
it was necessary to teach us.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of Step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Comparison to a parallel case (the gizzard and intestines).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ovary is obviously meat, so a ברייתא would never need to say it.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because some people do not eat the ovary, one might think it is not food, so the ברייתא had to teach that it counts as meat.

steps.title: A ברייתא: animals give birth at the time of day they mate
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that animals that mate by day give birth by day, those that mate by night give birth by night, and those that mate at any time give birth at any time.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: Whatever mates by day gives birth by day. Whatever mates by night gives birth by night. Whatever mates both by day and by night gives birth both by day and by night.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic by quoting a ברייתא about nature. It will soon connect this to eggs laid on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is that the time of mating matches the time of birth. The ברייתא sets up three groups: by day, by night, and at any time.

keyTerms.meaning: Born (for birds, the egg is laid)

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Whatever mates by day
is born by day.
Whatever mates by night
is born by night.

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁתַּשְׁמִישׁוֹ בֵּין בַּיּוֹם וּבֵין בַּלַּיְלָה —
phrases.english: Whatever mates both by day and by night
is born both by day and by night.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the egg-cluster discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The time of birth matches the time of mating: by day, by night, or both.

steps.title: Which creatures fit each group
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא names an example for each group: the chicken for day, the bat for night, and humans and similar creatures for both.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whatever mates by day is born by day: this is the chicken. Whatever mates by night is born by night: this is the bat. Whatever mates both by day and by night: this is a person and all that are like him.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains its three groups by naming an example of each.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The chicken is the key example for the coming הלכה. It mates by day, so it lays its eggs only by day.

keyTerms.meaning: And all that are like him

phrases.english: Whatever mates by day is born by day:
this is the chicken.
Whatever mates by night is born by night:
this is the bat.

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁתַּשְׁמִישׁוֹ בֵּין בַּיּוֹם וּבֵין בַּלַּיְלָה —
phrases.english: Whatever mates both by day and by night:
a person and all that are like him.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֹּל שֶׁתַּשְׁמִישׁוֹ בַּיּוֹם נוֹלָד בַּיּוֹם — זוֹ תַּרְנְגוֹלֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives examples for the general rule of Step 25.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The chicken lays by day, the bat gives birth by night, and humans give birth at any time.

steps.title: What difference does it make that chickens lay by day
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the line about the chicken and asks what practical difference it makes.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: Whatever mates by day is born by day, this is the chicken. What is the practical difference?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא focuses on the chicken line and asks why it matters for הלכה. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A fact about nature appears in a ברייתא, so the גמרא wants to know what הלכה depends on it.

keyTerms.meaning: What practical difference does it make?

phrases.english: The Master said:
Whatever mates by day is born by day:
this is the chicken.
What practical difference does it make?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: כֹּל שֶׁתַּשְׁמִישׁוֹ בַּיּוֹם נוֹלָד בַּיּוֹם — זוֹ תַּרְנְגוֹלֶת. לְמַאי נָפְקָא מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what הלכה follows from the chicken example in Step 26.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What הלכה depends on the fact that a chicken lays only by day.

steps.title: An egg found at dawn on יום טוב is permitted
steps.stepSummary: The difference is רב מרי בריה דרב כהנא's ruling. A nest that was empty on ערב יום טוב, with an egg found early the next morning, gives a permitted egg.
steps.simpleTranslation: It matters for the ruling of רב מרי בריה דרב כהנא. He said: If someone checked a chicken's nest on ערב יום טוב and found no egg, and the next morning he got up early and found an egg, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the practical result. Because chickens lay only by day, an egg found at dawn on יום טוב is permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The hen does not lay at night. So an egg found right at dawn is understood to have been laid on ערב יום טוב, and not during the night of יום טוב. That is why it is permitted.
steps.whatToRemember: Chickens lay only by day. So an egg found at dawn on יום טוב, in a nest that was empty on ערב יום טוב, is permitted (רב מרי בריה דרב כהנא).
steps.whyThisMatters: This connects a fact about nature to the main question of the מסכתא, which is whether an egg that appears on יום טוב is forbidden.

phrases.english: For that which Rav Mari son of Rav Kahana [said].

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב מָרִי בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב כָּהֲנָא:
phrases.english: As Rav Mari son of Rav Kahana said:
[If] he checked a chickens' nest
on the eve of Yom Tov
and did not find an egg in it,
and the next day he rose early
and found an egg in it,
it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 27 with a practical הלכה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The practical result is רב מרי בריה דרב כהנא's ruling that an egg found at dawn on יום טוב, in a nest that was empty on ערב יום טוב, is permitted.

steps.title: But he checked the nest
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב מרי: the owner checked the nest on ערב יום טוב and found nothing, so the egg must have been laid on יום טוב itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't he check the nest?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב מרי's ruling from the previous step. If the nest was checked and empty on ערב יום טוב, how can we say the egg came from yesterday?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב מרי's logic is that a hen lays only by day, so an egg found early in the morning was laid yesterday. But the person checked yesterday and saw no egg. So it seems the egg could only have appeared today, on יום טוב, and should be forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it so that…? (opens a challenge)

phrases.english: But didn't he check?!
phrases.notes: Refers to the case of רב מרי: the nest was checked and empty on ערב יום טוב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the case described in רב מרי's ruling
steps.kashyaTarget: רב מרי's ruling that the egg found early in the morning is permitted
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The nest was checked and empty on ערב יום טוב, so the egg seems to have been laid on יום טוב.

steps.title: He did not check well, or the egg came partly out and went back in
steps.stepSummary: Two answers: the check was not careful enough, or the egg mostly came out yesterday and slipped back in, which follows רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say that he did not check very carefully. And even if he did check carefully, say that most of the egg came out and went back in. This follows רבי יוחנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge in two ways, and each one explains how the egg can still count as yesterday's egg.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First answer: the egg was in the nest, and he simply missed it. Second answer: even with a careful check, the egg may have come mostly out of the hen on ערב יום טוב and then gone back inside. רבי יוחנן holds that such an egg counts as already 'born' before יום טוב, so it is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: Most of it came out and went back in
And this follows the view of רבי יוחנן

steps.confusionAlert: The egg did not hide in the nest in the second answer. It was still partly inside the hen. Because most of it had already come out before יום טוב, רבי יוחנן treats it as already 'born' then.

phrases.english: Say that he did not check very carefully.
phrases.notes: First answer: the egg was there and he missed it.

phrases.english: And even if he checked carefully,
say: most of it came out and went back in,
phrases.notes: This happened on ערב יום טוב.

phrases.english: and this follows רבי יוחנן.
phrases.notes: רבי יוחנן holds that an egg mostly out before יום טוב counts as already laid, so it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 29
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the facts of the case (two options)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: An empty nest on ערב יום טוב proves the egg was laid on יום טוב.
steps.terutzMaskana: Either the check missed the egg, or the egg mostly came out before יום טוב. Either way it belongs to ערב יום טוב.

steps.title: רב rules that such an egg is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings רב's ruling that an egg found in the morning, in a nest that was empty the evening before, is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But רבי יוסי בן שאול said in the name of רב: If one checked a hen's nest on ערב יום טוב and found no egg, and the next day he got up early and found an egg, it is forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב מרי with a ruling of רב about the very same case, and רב reaches the opposite result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The facts match רב מרי's case exactly: an empty nest at night and an egg early the next morning. רב forbids the egg, which suggests a hen can lay at night. That contradicts רב מרי and the ברייתא about the hen laying only by day.

phrases.english: Is that so?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן שָׁאוּל אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: But didn't רבי יוסי בן שאול say in the name of רב:

phrases.aramaic: בָּדַק בְּקִנָּה שֶׁל תַּרְנְגוֹלֶת מֵעֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב
phrases.english: If one checked a hen's nest on the eve of the Festival
and did not find an egg in it,
and the next day he rose early and found an egg in it —
it is forbidden!
phrases.notes: This implies the egg may have been laid during the night of יום טוב.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי? וְהָא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן שָׁאוּל אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge against רב מרי, this time from a contradicting ruling
steps.kashyaTarget: רב מרי's permission, and the idea that a hen never lays at night
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב forbids the egg in the identical case, so a hen must be able to lay at night.

steps.title: רב is speaking of an egg absorbed from the earth
steps.stepSummary: רב's case is a hen whose egg came from the earth rather than from a rooster. Such an egg can be laid at night.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it is a case where the hen absorbed from the earth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by saying רב is talking about a different kind of egg.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule that day-mating creatures give birth by day applies only to eggs that come from mating with a rooster. An egg formed without a rooster, 'from the earth', has no such timing. It can be laid at night, so רב forbids it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the key distinction for the rest of the סוגיא. An egg from a rooster is laid only by day. An egg 'from the earth' can be laid at any time.

phrases.english: There it is where it absorbed from the earth.
phrases.notes: The egg was not formed through a rooster, so the day-only rule does not apply.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction of step 31
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב and רב מרי argue about the same case.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב's case involves an egg from the earth, which can be laid at night. רב מרי's case does not.

steps.title: Maybe רב מרי's hen also absorbed from the earth
steps.stepSummary: If an egg from the earth can come at night, then רב מרי's egg might be one too, so why permit it?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, in רב מרי's case too, say that the hen absorbed from the earth!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the last answer back against רב מרי himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We now know that some eggs can be laid at night. In רב מרי's case, how do we know the egg was not that kind? The doubt should make his egg forbidden too.

phrases.english: If so,
in רב מרי's case too,
say it absorbed from the earth?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי דְּרַב מָרִי נָמֵי אֵימָא מֵאַרְעָא סָפְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 32 by applying it to רב מרי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Any hen might hold an egg from the earth, which can be laid at night.

steps.title: In רב מרי's case a rooster is with the hen
steps.stepSummary: רב מרי speaks of a hen that has a rooster with her, so her egg comes from the rooster.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a case where there is a male with her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that רב מרי's hen lives with a rooster.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A rooster is present, so we assume the egg came from mating. Mating happens by day, so laying happens by day too. That is why the morning egg belongs to yesterday.

phrases.english: Where there is a male with her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 33
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב מרי's hen might have an egg from the earth.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב מרי's hen has a rooster, so the egg comes from mating.

steps.title: Even with a rooster, maybe she absorbed from the earth
steps.stepSummary: A rooster being nearby does not prove the egg came from him. She could still have absorbed from the earth.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even where there is a male, say she absorbed from the earth!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the last answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The presence of a rooster makes it possible that the egg came from mating, but does it rule out an egg from the earth? If not, the doubt remains, and the egg should be forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: In a case where there is

phrases.english: Even where there is a male,
say she absorbed from the earth!

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּדְאִיכָּא זָכָר נָמֵי, אֵימָא מֵאַרְעָא סָפְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 34
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a rooster's presence settles the matter
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A rooster nearby does not prove the egg did not come from the earth.

steps.title: A tradition: with a rooster nearby, a hen does not absorb from the earth
steps.stepSummary: רבינא cites a received tradition that wherever a rooster is present, a hen does not form an egg from the earth.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: We have a tradition that wherever there is a male, the hen does not absorb from the earth.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא settles the question with a known tradition about nature.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not a logical proof but a received fact, which is why it is introduced with 'גמירי'. Once a rooster is around, an egg from the earth is not a possibility. So רב מרי's egg must come from mating and was laid by day.
steps.whatToRemember: An egg from a rooster is laid only by day, so it can be permitted when found in the morning (רב מרי). An egg 'from the earth' can be laid at night, so it is forbidden (רב). A rooster's presence rules out an egg from the earth.

phrases.english: Ravina said: It is learned as a tradition:
anywhere that there is a male —
she does not absorb from the earth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 35 and closes the challenge cycle
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A hen with a rooster might still have an egg from the earth.
steps.terutzMaskana: By tradition, a hen with a rooster never absorbs from the earth.

steps.title: How near must the rooster be?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the distance within which a rooster counts as being 'with' the hen.
steps.simpleTranslation: And up to how far?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that a rooster's presence matters, the גמרא asks how close he needs to be.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא's tradition depends on a rooster being 'present'. The גמרא wants a practical measure of distance for applying it.

keyTerms.meaning: And up to how much / how far?

phrases.english: And up to how far?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a measure needed to apply the tradition in step 36
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The distance within which a rooster counts as present with the hen.

steps.title: רב גמדא begins to give the measure
steps.stepSummary: רב גמדא, in the name of רב, starts to define the distance. The rest of his answer continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב גמדא said in the name of רב: Anywhere that…
steps.whatsHappening: The answer begins here, but the sentence is cut off and finishes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב גמדא brings a definition from רב. Only the opening words, 'anywhere that', appear on this amud. The actual measure comes on the next amud.

Anywhere that…
